stem: Represent the relation $x - 2y + 4 = 0$ graphically by dragging two points. Then read the slope of the line and the length of the part of the y-axis between the origin and the line.
solution: The y-intercept is $b = 2$: the line crosses the y-axis at (0, 2), so the length is 2.
Plot (0, 2), then go 2 right and 1 up to get (2, 3), and draw the line through them.
notes: m=1/2 is allowed (reciprocal of a whole number). Reading the coefficient of x as the slope and c as the intercept gives m=1, b=4, which usually fires off-target. slope-inverted (m=2, from mixing a and b) is not mapped, since it does not cleanly match either misconception. Any two points on the correct line are accepted.
